channel.title: Modal Resonance Writing
channel.description: Perspectives on AI systems, privacy, and evaluation from the Modal Resonance team.

item.title: Towards technical evaluation of AI model anonymity
item.description: We tested the CNIL's PANAME library, fine-tuning a Llama 3.2 1B model on Enron emails to measure how much sanitizing training data reduces membership inference attack success.
item.author: Omar Ali Fdal, Matteo Giomi

item.title: IEEE report on synthetic data: privacy risks, metrics, and governance.
item.description: The IEEE Industry Connections 2025 report on structured synthetic data, co-authored by Matteo Giomi, examines the legal, technical, and governance dimensions of synthetic data and establishes that anonymity cannot be assumed from generation alone.
item.author: Matteo Giomi, Omar Ali Fdal

item.title: Privacy risks evaluation at scale: NIST's Collaborative Research Cycle
item.description: Applying Anonymeter to over 150 de-identified datasets from the NIST Collaborative Research Cycle shows that no current synthesis algorithm achieves residual privacy risk below a few percentage points, and that algorithm choice can change measured risk by an order of magnitude.
item.author: Matteo Giomi, Omar Ali Fdal

item.title: Empirical Privacy Risk Assessment in Tabular Synthetic Data
item.description: Anonymeter is an open-source framework for measuring privacy risk in synthetic tabular data, published at PoPETs 2023 and evaluated positively by France's CNIL.
item.author: Matteo Giomi, Omar Ali Fdal

item.title: Benchmarking Open-Source PII Detectors
item.description: We benchmarked three open-source PII detectors (Microsoft Presidio, GLiNER, and OpenAI's Privacy Filter) on detection accuracy and throughput across two datasets and six entity types. OPF leads out-of-the-box on a GPU, Presidio wins on CPU and pattern-rich entities, GLiNER is the most flexible to configure.
item.author: Matteo Giomi, Omar Ali Fdal

item.title: Mapping Privacy Risk Across the AI Lifecycle
item.description: A structured breakdown of where privacy risk lives across the four phases of the AI lifecycle, and what genuinely changes with generative AI versus traditional ML.
item.author: Omar Ali Fdal, Matteo Giomi
